content:
Lina: Heads up — Next.js middleware deploy is failing for our users who import the SDK directly. Error in Vercel logs: `ReferenceError: require is not defined`.

Owen: That's because middleware runs in the Edge runtime (no CommonJS). Did you import the package main entry? Many packages default to CJS.

Lina: Yeah `import { client } from 'redwood-sdk'` blows up. We tried `await import('redwood-sdk')` dynamically and that works at runtime but TS complains during build.

Nina: Typical options: publish a dedicated ES module for edge (e.g. dist/edge/index.mjs) and expose it via `exports` or a direct path. Also ship types for that path so tsc resolves them.

Owen: Example exports block we used in a different project: 

```
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```

Then middleware does `await import('redwood-sdk/edge')`. No runtime error.

Lina: Interesting. We tried `redwood-sdk/dist/edge/index.mjs` explicit path and it worked, but our linter and bundle analyzer flagged the deep import. Also our types broke.

Victor: To fix types, add a `types` entry for the edge build and/or use `typesVersions` to map imports: 

```
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"typesVersions": {
  "*": {
    "./edge": ["dist/edge/index.d.ts"]
  }
}
```

That lets TS find types for `redwood-sdk/edge`.

sdk-bot: CI alert: 1769551260 — edge bundle missing in published tgz. Please update release pipeline.

Nina: Another gotcha: transitive deps. Even if our package is ESM, a dependency that requires `fs` or does `module.exports` will break in Edge. Two approaches: 1) make the edge bundle replace or shim node-only deps, 2) vendor small helpers into the edge build.

Owen: For retry logic, server SDKs often depend on `setTimeout` or timers. Edge supports a subset of globals — avoid relying on Node-only timers or `process`. Use AbortController + fetch-friendly retry code.

Lina: Any DX pattern to keep imports nice in user code? We want `import { Inference } from 'redwood-sdk'` to just work everywhere.

Victor: That's ideal but tricky. Conditional exports can help (exports.import -> offers ESM for browsers/edge) plus a tiny top-level module file that re-exports `./edge` when detected. Example top-level `index.mjs`: `export * from './edge/index.mjs'` and `index.cjs` for node. Next will prefer the import field.

Nina: Also document it. Users confused by deep imports. Add an example Next middleware recipe to the README and an `examples/next-middleware` with a tiny `middleware.ts` showing `await import('redwood-sdk/edge')` and a typed declaration so tsc is happy.

Lina: OK — for now we patched our app to use the explicit edge path and added `declare module 'redwood-sdk/edge'` to `global.d.ts`. CI passes locally. Will wait for SDK team release.

Owen: I'll file a short SDK issue: add edge bundle, publish types for the edge path, and note limitations (no node-only deps).

Lina: Thanks all. Small wins: dynamic import + typed ambient module works as a short-term fix.
